issues.item: Compulsive Exercise: I push myself to exercise excessively
issues.explanation: Compulsive exercise is weakly integrated with the rest of the profile. The other selected items cluster around hypervigilance, dissociation, memory disorganisation, and danger-based appraisals after terrorism. Excessive exercise does not clearly serve or connect to those symptoms, making it look like a strategy for a different presentation unless additional context were present.

issues.item: Life Not Worth Living: I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
issues.explanation: 'Life Not Worth Living' is disproportionately severe relative to the rest of the selected profile and is not well supported by the surrounding appraisals. The other appraisals focus on danger and bodily unreliability, while the threat/memory items emphasize hyperarousal and fragmented recall. This suicidal-hopelessness appraisal can occur in PTSD, but here it stands out as insufficiently linked to the rest of the formulation and item set.

vignette: Maria, a 24-year-old Latina woman who works at a warehouse, has been experiencing significant distress since witnessing an act of terrorism at her workplace last year. The traumatic event left deep psychological scars that have progressively affected her daily life. The incident began one ordinary day when Maria was working her shift at the warehouse. Suddenly, there were explosions and shouts, followed by chaos as people tried to flee. Amidst the confusion, she recalls flashes of panic and fear but struggles to piece together many details. What remains vivid are moments of intense violence and the sound of screams, which have left indelible marks on her psyche. Since then, Maria has come to believe that the world is a dangerous place where threats lurk around every corner. This belief manifests in her constant need for vigilance; she finds it hard to feel safe at night or when sudden movements occur nearby. The intensity of this feeling has led her to adopt various maladaptive strategies. She avoids making eye contact with others, dissociates by deliberately blanking out, and constantly scans her surroundings for any signs of potential danger. Maria's struggles with memory are particularly pronounced; there are parts of the event that she simply cannot recall, no matter how hard she tries. When she does manage to remember certain aspects, intense rage often surges through her. This inability to fully process what happened has made it difficult for Maria to communicate about the experience, leaving her feeling frustrated and isolated. Her negative appraisals have reinforced these maladaptive behaviors. The belief that her body is unreliable means she distrusts physical sensations like fear or anxiety, leading her to feel even more on edge. This hypervigilance further exacerbates her startle response, making her jumpy and easily startled. Over time, the cycle of negative thoughts and heightened threat perception has led Maria to withdraw from social interactions, fearing that others might trigger memories of the event. In her daily work at the warehouse, these symptoms have become increasingly problematic. The constant scanning for threats makes it hard for her to concentrate on tasks, leading to frequent errors in inventory management. Her coworkers have noticed changes in her behavior and sometimes express concern, but Maria's distrust makes it difficult for her to open up about what she is going through. Maria has come to believe that the only way to cope with the overwhelming sense of danger is by constantly monitoring her environment and avoiding situations that might trigger memories. This hypervigilance has created a vicious cycle where her fear feeds into her maladaptive strategies, which in turn reinforce her negative appraisals about the world's dangers. The culmination of these experiences brought Maria to seek help. Her work performance had declined significantly, and she was struggling to maintain basic social connections. She is most afraid that she will continue to spiral downward without understanding why she feels so unsafe all the time. At the same time, she hopes for a way to regain control over her life and find peace. Maria's journey towards healing begins with recognizing how her negative appraisals have shaped her current behaviors and perceptions. Through therapy, she aims to break free from the cycle of fear and mistrust that has taken hold of her life.
